success_means: Beat progressively stronger perfect-play opponents at Connect 4. A policy has mastered the task when it wins or draws at least 90% of games against every opponent on the ladder, including one that plays perfectly six moves deep.

procedure.opponents: negamax search with alpha-beta pruning over the real rules, at fixed depths 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 (an opponent of exactly known strength, not an estimate)
procedure.openings: 14 fixed opening sequences (7 of one move, 7 of two moves), chosen once with a recorded seed and frozen
procedure.seats: each opening played twice, once with the policy moving first and once second
procedure.determinism: the opponents and openings are fixed, so the only variation between runs is the policy itself

scoring.headline: mean of the six per-opponent scores, in [0, 1]
scoring.frontier_depth: the shallowest opponent not yet beaten 90% of the time — reports which opponent is next

mastery.note: the headline average can be lifted by easy rungs, so mastery requires the threshold at EVERY depth

inference_rule: The policy reads the position once and commits to a move. No lookahead, no search, no assistance. Lookahead during training is unrestricted; see learning rules 1 and 2.
notes: Deliberately absolute rather than relative. An earlier project measured only wins against previous versions of itself, promoted 32 times, and never knew whether it was any good. A fixed opponent of known strength is what makes a score mean something years later.
